scenarioStory.history: Patient was asleep when a kitchen fire spread through her apartment. She was found by fire crews in a smoke-filled bedroom and carried out. She is coughing, her voice is progressively hoarser, and she has visible partial and full-thickness burns to her face, neck, and both forearms.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew finds a 39-year-old female just extracted from a smoke-filled apartment. She is alert, coughing, with soot around her mouth and nose, singed nasal hairs, a hoarsening voice, and visible burns to her face, neck, and forearms. → Early RSI performed for airway burn: Recognizing the sentinel signs of an airway burn, the crew performs early RSI before swelling progresses to complete obstruction. → Fluids and burn care initiated: With the airway secured, the crew estimates TBSA, begins fluid resuscitation per the Rule of Ten, dresses the burns, and prepares for burn center transport.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Burns and hoarse voice after being pulled from a house fire

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew finds a 39-year-old female just extracted from a smoke-filled apartment. She is alert, coughing, with soot around her mouth and nose, singed nasal hairs, a hoarsening voice, and visible burns to her face, neck, and forearms.

scenarioEvents.name: Early RSI performed for airway burn
scenarioEvents.description: Recognizing the sentinel signs of an airway burn, the crew performs early RSI before swelling progresses to complete obstruction.
relatedChecklist: Recognize stridor and hoarse voice as sentinel signs of a significant airway burn
Preoxygenate with high-flow O2 and positive pressure for 2 minutes before RSI
RSI: fentanyl 65 mcg IV (65 kg × 1 mcg/kg), etomidate 13 mg IV (65 kg × 0.2 mg/kg), rocuronium 65 mg IV (65 kg × 1 mg/kg)
Intubate with 7.5 mm ETT (adult female sizing), confirm with waveform capnography

scenarioEvents.name: Fluids and burn care initiated
scenarioEvents.description: With the airway secured, the crew estimates TBSA, begins fluid resuscitation per the Rule of Ten, dresses the burns, and prepares for burn center transport.
relatedChecklist: Estimate TBSA at 40% (rounded) using Rule of Nines, excluding first-degree burns
Initiate LR at 400 mL/hr (40% TBSA × 10; 65 kg patient, within the 40–80 kg bracket)
Remove jewelry and wet clothing, cover burns with dry dressing, leave blisters intact, no gels/ointments
Apply warming measures to prevent systemic heat loss
Transport to burn/trauma center given airway involvement and TBSA > 10%

scenarioEvents.name: Airway management delayed
scenarioEvents.description: The crew focuses on burn wound care and pain control while the airway burn progresses, and stridor worsens toward complete obstruction.
relatedChecklist: Recognize impending complete obstruction; perform surgical airway when oxygenation/ventilation cannot be achieved
